newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK retail sales seen up 13 pct in 1997 - Lehman.
newsitem.headline: HK retail sales seen up 13 pct in 1997 - Lehman.

text.p: Hong Kong's nominal retail sales should jump 13 percent in 1997 on the back of a resurgent local economy, investment bank Lehman Brothers forecast.

"We are being conservative when we tip a 13 percent increase in retail sales. Retail sales may recover by 15 or even 16 percent if the economy performs well," said Miron Mushkat, Lehman's chief economist for the Asia Pacific.
After two years of economic slowdown, rising propert prices, a stable interest rate outlook and solid growth in gross domestic income was likely to boost retail sales, Lehman said.
"Economic forces have recently reversed direction and are now driving consumer demand upward. The recovery in durable sales, like motor vehicles and parts, illustrates the point.
"This recovery has just begun...and is expected to gain mmentum in the months ahead," Mushkat said.
Retail sales grew eight percent in value and three percent in volume in November 1996. For 1995 as a whole, retail sales rose five percent in value but dropped one percent in volume.
